title: Chemical Depletion of Phagocytic Hemocytes in Anopheles gambiae Using Clodronate Liposomes
author: Kwon, Smith
materials: In this step, use of gene expression analysis via real-time qPCR will confirm phagocyte depletion following the injection of clodronate liposomes.14.Isolate total RNA from LP- or CLD-treated mosquitoes.a.One day post-injection of LP or CLD, collect ∼10 individual mosquitoes in a 1.5 ml Eppendorf tube for RNA isolation. The samples can be either stored at −80°C or immediately processed.b.Add 500 μL of TRIzol reagent to each sample and homogenize with a motorized pestle until any large tissues are gone.c.Add an additional 500 μL of TRIzol reagent to the homogenized samples and incubate for 5 min at RT.d.Centrifuge samples at 12,000 x g for 15 min at 4°C using a refrigerated centrifuge and transfer the supernatant to a new 1.5 ml tube.e.Add 200 μL of chloroform to each sample and shake vigorously for 15 s.f.Incubate samples at RT for 2 to 3 min, then centrifuge at 12,000 x g for 15 min at 4°C.g.Remove the upper aqueous clear layer and transfer to a new 1.5 ml tube.h.Add 250 μL of isopropyl alcohol and 250 μL of 0.8 M sodium citrate/1.2 M NaCl. Incubate samples at RT for 10 min.CRITICAL: The addition of the 0.8 M sodium citrate/ 1.2 M NaCl solution is absolutely necessary for whole mosquito samples. Without this step pigments from the whole mosquito lysate will form a reddish-brown RNA pellet that will interfere with RNA quantification and downstream PCR steps.i.Centrifuge samples at 12,000 x g for 10 min at 4°C. When complete, a small whitish RNA pellet should be visible. Carefully remove all of the supernatant using a narrow bore pipette tip.j.Wash the RNA pellet using 500 μL of 70% of ethanol and centrifuge at 7,500 x g for 5 min at 4°C. Repeat this step.k.Remove the ethanol supernatant and air dry the RNA pellet for 5–10 min.l.Resuspend RNA pellets with 40 μL of RNase-free water. Vortex samples to completely dissolve pellets.Note: Samples can be optionally incubated at 65°C using a water bath or heating block to help resuspend the RNA pellets.m.Treat the RNA sample with DNase to remove any gDNA present by adding 0.1 volume 10X TURBO DNase buffer and 1 μL of TURBO DNase. Incubate in a 37°C water bath for 30 min.n.Add DNase inactivation reagent (0.1 volume) and incubate at RT for 5 min.o.Centrifuge at 12,000 x g for 2 min at 4°C. Transfer the RNA (supernatant) to a clean 1.5 ml tube.p.Measure the RNA concentration using a NanoDrop spectrophotometer.Store the RNA samples at −80°C or proceed directly to cDNA synthesis.15.Perform cDNA synthesis using the RevertAid First Strand cDNA Synthesis kit according to the manufacturer’s protocol.a.Add 2 μg of total RNA (volume will vary), 1 μL of 100 μM oligo dT, 1 μL of 100 μM random hexamer and nuclease free water to a total of 12 μL in a 0.2 ml PCR tube.b.Incubate the mixture at 65°C for 5 min using a thermocycler. Quickly spin in a PCR mini centrifuge and chill on ice.c.Add 4 μL of 5X reaction buffer, 1 μL of RNase inhibitor, 2 μL of 10 mM dNTPs and 1 μL of reverse transcriptase to each sample. Incubate at RT (∼25°C) for 5 min.d.Incubate samples at 42°C for 1 h, then 70°C for 5 min to terminate the reaction.e.Dilute the cDNA (1:5) in nuclease free water and keep at −20°C.16.Perform real-time qPCR analysis from the prepared cDNA of LP- and CLD-treated mosquitoes.a.Evaluate the expression of Eater and Nimrod B2, genes expressed in phagocytic granulocyte populations in An. gambiae,1,9 to serve as an indirect method to evaluate cell numbers.b.The inclusion of rpS7 (or similar housekeeping gene) should be included as an internal reference gene to standardize gene expression between samples.Note: The use of an additional gene, such as PPO1, can also be included to represent non-target oenocytoid populations.10c.Prepare the real-time qPCR reaction with PowerUp SYBRGreen Master Mix using a QuantStudio 3 Real-Time PCR System.Note: Prepare a larger volume of real-time qPCR master mix than needed for all of the reactions to prevent running out of the mixture during pipetting. This will produce more consistent and accurate results between sample replicates.Real-time qPCR cycling conditionStepsTemperatureTimeCyclesInitial Denaturation95 °C10 min1Denaturation95 °C15 s40 cyclesAnnealing65 °C1 minHold4 °CForever

steps.title: Prepare hemolymph perfusion needles
steps.instruction: Pull glass capillary needles using a Sutter P‑97 (or P‑2000) micropipette puller with the following starting settings: Heat‑Pull Velocity 320, Time 100, Pressure 100, 200, 500 (adjust as needed). Pull 5–10 needles, break the tip under a microscope with forceps immediately before use, and test flow to ensure liquid only bubbles out under applied pressure and does not leak. Verify needle quality by injecting 1X PBS into mosquitoes and confirming survival.

steps.title: Prepare anticoagulant buffer
steps.instruction: Make an anticoagulant buffer at pH ≈ 5.5–6.0. Prepare batches of 10–100 mL, aliquot 1.5 mL portions into 1.5 mL tubes, and store at –20 °C until needed.

steps.title: Isolate total RNA from treated mosquitoes
steps.instruction: One day after injection of liposome (LP) or clodronate (CLD) liposomes, collect ~10 individual mosquitoes per sample in a 1.5 mL tube (store at –80 °C or process immediately). Add 500 µL TRIzol, homogenize with a motorized pestle, add another 500 µL TRIzol, incubate 5 min at room temperature (RT). Centrifuge 12,000 × g for 15 min at 4 °C, transfer supernatant to a new tube, add 200 µL chloroform, shake 15 s, incubate 2–3 min at RT, centrifuge 12,000 × g for 15 min at 4 °C, transfer the aqueous layer, add 250 µL isopropanol and 250 µL 0.8 M sodium citrate/1.2 M NaCl, incubate 10 min at RT, centrifuge 12,000 × g for 10 min at 4 °C, discard supernatant, wash pellet with 500 µL 70 % ethanol, centrifuge 7,500 × g for 5 min at 4 °C, repeat wash, air‑dry pellet 5–10 min, resuspend in 40 µL RNase‑free water (optional 65 °C incubation to aid dissolution).

steps.title: DNase treat and quantify RNA
steps.instruction: Add 0.1 volume 10X TURBO DNase buffer and 1 µL TURBO DNase to each RNA sample, incubate 30 min at 37 °C. Add 0.1 volume DNase inactivation reagent, incubate 5 min at RT, centrifuge 12,000 × g for 2 min at 4 °C, transfer supernatant to a clean tube. Measure RNA concentration with a NanoDrop and store at –80 °C or proceed to cDNA synthesis.

steps.title: Synthesize cDNA from RNA
steps.instruction: Using the RevertAid First Strand cDNA Synthesis kit, combine 2 µg total RNA, 1 µL 100 µM oligo‑dT, 1 µL 100 µM random hexamer, and nuclease‑free water to a total volume of 12 µL in a 0.2 mL PCR tube. Incubate 65 °C for 5 min, spin briefly, chill on ice. Add 4 µL 5X reaction buffer, 1 µL RNase inhibitor, 2 µL 10 mM dNTPs, and 1 µL reverse transcriptase; incubate 5 min at RT (~25 °C). Then incubate 42 °C for 1 h, followed by 70 °C for 5 min to terminate. Dilute the cDNA 1:5 with nuclease‑free water and store at –20 °C.

steps.title: Perform real‑time qPCR
steps.instruction: Set up qPCR reactions with PowerUp SYBR‑Green Master Mix on a QuantStudio 3 system to assess expression of Eater, Nimrod B2 (phagocytic granulocyte markers) and rpS7 (housekeeping). Optionally include PPO1 for non‑target oenocytoids. Prepare a master mix volume larger than the total reaction volume needed. Cycling conditions: 95 °C 10 min initial denaturation; 40 cycles of 95 °C 15 s denaturation, 65 °C 1 min annealing/extension; hold at 4 °C forever.

steps.title: Analyze qPCR data
steps.instruction: Normalize target gene Ct values to rpS7, calculate relative expression using the 2⁻ΔΔCt method, combine independent biological replicates, and assess significance with a Student’s t‑test in GraphPad Prism.

steps.title: Prepare mosquitoes for flow cytometry
steps.instruction: One day after LP or CLD injection, cold‑anesthetize mosquitoes on ice. Inject each mosquito with 69 nL of red fluorescent carboxylate‑modified 1 µm microspheres at a final concentration of 2 % (vol/vol) in 1X PBS. Allow mosquitoes to recover for 30 min at 27 °C.

steps.title: Perfuse hemolymph and fix cells
steps.instruction: Perfuse hemolymph from ~40 mosquitoes per treatment using anticoagulant (AC) buffer, collecting directly into 1.5 mL tubes on ice. Add an equal volume of 4 % paraformaldehyde (1:1), incubate 1 h at 4 °C, then centrifuge 2000 × g for 5 min at 4 °C and discard supernatant.

steps.title: Wash and stain cell samples
steps.instruction: Wash cells with 1 mL 1X PBS, centrifuge 2000 × g for 5 min at 4 °C; repeat the wash. Stain the pellet in 1X PBS containing FITC‑WGA (1:5000) and DRAQ5 (1:1000); incubate overnight (~16 h) at 4 °C. After incubation, centrifuge, discard supernatant, wash twice more with 1X PBS (centrifuge as above), then resuspend in 200 µL 1X PBS and transfer to flow cytometry tubes.

steps.title: Run flow cytometry and acquire data
steps.instruction: Analyze stained samples on a BD FACSCanto (or comparable) cytometer according to standard settings for detecting FITC‑WGA and red fluorescent beads.

steps.title: Gate phagocytic hemocytes in FlowJo
steps.instruction: In FlowJo, open the .fcs files (unstained, bead‑only, LP, CLD). Set FSC thresholds to define bead size, use unstained cells to set cut‑offs for positive WGA and DRAQ5 signals, then gate double‑positive (bead + WGA) events. Calculate the percentage of phagocytic hemocytes for each sample.

description: Our protocol describes the application and use of clodronate liposomes to study mosquito immune cell function in Anopheles gambiae,1 although similar approaches have been recently applied in other arthropod systems.2,3,4,5 Herein, we outline procedures for liposome injection and subsequent methods to validate phagocyte depletion using microscopy, gene expression, and flow cytometry techniques.
